title: a-node-holds-one-claim
intention: A TREE NODE HOLDS ONE CLAIM, NOT EIGHT. A verdict deposits as its PARTS — one node per verdict and per disposition, each with its own honest vector — and the whole verdict is DERIVED BY READ from the parts, never stored twice. This clears ticket the-deposit-rides-the-read (Stone A), whose verdict has stood pending since 2026-07-29 because its single rendering is 11283 chars against a measured ~7400-char embed ceiling.
why:
THE CEILING WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM — IT WAS THE MESSENGER. MEASURED 2026-07-29: A's verdict is 11283 chars as one node (1.5x over), while its largest single part is 2097 and its smallest 1267 — every part fits with 3.5x headroom. So the wall is GRANULARITY, not capacity, and the embed host refusing was Law 3 doing its job: it surfaced a node-shape error. Look at what one vector over 11283 chars of eight distinct claims actually IS — a centroid of eight unrelated things, pointing nowhere in particular. Eight vectors each pointing at one claim is MORE ACCURATE, not merely smaller. The monolith was already the wrong shape before it was too big; truncation would have hidden the finding and split the vector from its content, which is why it was refused rather than trimmed.

AND THE CLOSE MECHANISM ITSELF IS CAPPED. Stone C's verdict came in at 6418 of ~7400 — I got it under the ceiling by writing DELIBERATELY TERSE evidence, by hand, at close. That is an operator compensating for a missing physics, and the next stone over is a coin toss. [[solidify-the-layer-below]]: a problem surfaced in a lower layer (the deposit/embed seam) and future builds are already unconsciously compensating for it, which is how a 'proven' whole quietly stops being proven. Every subsequent stone's close rides this seam, so it is not Stone A's private blocker — it is the close mechanism's blocker, and it goes in front of the queue.
traces_to: Law 1 — the whole is a READ-PROJECTION of its parts, derived not stored; and without this, every future close re-derives the same workaround (an operator hand-trimming prose to fit a ceiling nobody declared)
Law 3 — the ceiling is measured (7403 embedded / 7447 refused; A at 11283; parts 1267-2097), and the retrieval improvement is labelled a HYPOTHESIS until walked
Law 7 — the pending deposit stayed LOUD and standing rather than being trimmed into a coherent-looking lie; a record of truth never collapses an error
Law 8 — truncating to fit would be a hollow pass: a vector describing bytes the node does not hold

the librarian's tenure loop — parts are the unit of REUSE (node_id_for is a content hash), so a recurring disposition shape dedupes into one node with many corroborations; a monolith can never dedupe, every stone's verdict being unique by construction

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate: teeth beside the code (cairn/machines/chart/proofs/test_chart_verdict.py extends; the deposit door's own teeth in cairn/devices/librarian/proofs/ must all still green), under the tester with the netns seal. THE PARTS RENDERER: one pure function yields [(kind, content), ...] from the artifact and REMAINS THE SINGLE SOURCE for both what is embedded and what is deposited (the 'one rendering, no drift' why, held per node). THE BOUND IS TOKENS, NOT CHARS: the pre-flight asks the host for prompt_eval_count rather than guessing from length — my 7400-char check was expedient, not correct (chars-per-token swings with punctuation-dense prose). A part over the token bound REFUSES LOUDLY and stands pending, exactly as the monolith did; it is never split further silently. THE COUNT CHECK IS THE PHYSICS: a composition read that recovers fewer parts than the berth declares REFUSES rather than returning a short verdict — this is what makes provenance-append a sibling instead of a prerequisite (see dependencies). LIVE GATE: Stone A's standing pending verdict drains and lands as parts on the first door read — which is a live fire ALREADY WAITING ON THE LEDGER, not one this stone has to manufacture, and it re-opens A's own path from LEARNME to an honest PROVED. Then the NEXT close authored through the new shape, whichever stone that is, must need no operator hand-trimming to fit.
falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: (1) any part is deposited whose content is not byte-identical to what was embedded for it (the drift this stone must not introduce while fixing granularity); (2) a composition read returns a verdict SHORT of the parts its berth declares, silently — it must refuse (a quietly-short verdict is strictly worse than the loud pending line we have today); (3) a part over the bound is split, summarised, or truncated to fit rather than refused; (4) the whole is persisted anywhere as well as its parts (a second record of truth); (5) an existing monolith node is rewritten or deleted to 'migrate' it — history is append-only and the tree is allowed to be mixed-granularity; (6) the bound is still asked of a character count rather than the host's token count. KILL CONDITION (a3, honest): if constrain finds NOTHING reads the reassembled whole, the composition half is speculative and this stone shrinks to parts-only — that is a win, not a failure of the cast.
falsifier.horizon: re-read when: the tenure loop lands (parts become corroborated nodes and provenance-append retires the count-check's refusal path); a walk is measured over the split tree (a1 stops being a hypothesis and becomes a number, either way); a second artifact class wants the same treatment (the stage packets deposit as monoliths today and merely HAPPEN to fit — 6418 of 7400 on C is the warning); the embed model changes and the token bound moves.

chart_notes.orient: NOTE THE KNOWN CENSUS LIMIT before trusting any inspector reading here: orient's device_census is scoped to cairn/ (measured at skills-ride-the-chokepoint's close, FINDING 1). It sees chart and librarian, so this stone is in jurisdiction — but do not assume coverage anywhere else
chart_notes.constrain: SETTLE a3 FIRST, because it can shrink the stone: does anything READ the reassembled whole verdict, or only the parts? The walk retrieves parts; a human reading a stone's verdict wants the whole — but is there such a reader TODAY? If not, build parts-only ([[build-minimal-grow-against-need]]) and let composition arrive with its first real consumer. Also settle: what IS a part (is `disposition.by` alone a good node, or does a part need its piece+expect for context to be walkable?), and whether the parts renderer emits the claim VERBATIM as it does today (it must — the berth is the record of truth and retyping is how drift enters)
chart_notes.survey: what deposit_learning / deposit_packet already do per-stage (every stage packet is ALSO a monolith today and merely happens to fit — C at 6418/7400 says how close); how the tree walk behaves against mixed-granularity siblings, since C's monolith stays (a4); whether prompt_eval_count is already surfaced through inference_domain's metered path or needs asking for; git's object model as the pattern precedent, read for what it settles rather than re-derived
chart_notes.decompose: candidate split is (i) parts renderer + token bound, (ii) plural ledger + composition read. Confirm they share a PROOF STORY and not merely a theme — if they do not, that is the finding that earns the split (the rule nothing-rides-loose's decompose note states). My prior: one stone, because the count check straddles both halves and is the physics that makes the ordering safe
chart_notes.triage: the parts renderer is the half that clears A and unblocks B's close; the composition read is the half a3 might kill outright. Order accordingly — and do NOT let the composition half hold the parts half hostage
chart_notes.hypothesize: state a1 AS A LABELLED HYPOTHESIS: that per-part vectors retrieve better than the monolith's centroid. It is the WHY of the whole stone and it is UNMEASURED. Instrument it: walk the same request against A's monolith-shaped question before and after, and record the result EVEN IF IT DISAPPOINTS — a1 disappointing would still leave the ceiling cleared, so the stone survives a red here, but the WHY would need rewriting and that is worth knowing
chart_notes.validate: the instrument, run twice, plus the live fire that is ALREADY STANDING: A's pending verdict on the ledger drains and lands as parts, and A crosses LEARNME -> PROVED honestly. MEASURED CORRECTION at cast (Law 3 over a remembered claim): I had believed a-voyage-names-its-ticket was held at LEARNME awaiting a sibling's forward crossing and would therefore be the first close AUTHORED through this shape. The disk says otherwise — it stands at TICKETME with its chart pending, i.e. never built. So the second live fire is 'the next close, whichever stone it is, needs no hand-trimming', and it is not scheduled by this stone
